title: Neighbors and coworkers
hook: Most people will never read a book about Islam. They'll just live next to you, or work with you.

screens.text: The family next door. The guy at the next desk. The classmate in your group project. To them, *you* might be the only Muslim they know. No pressure. Just a chance.

**Neighbors matter a lot in Islam.** The Prophet ﷺ said the angel **Jibril** kept urging him to be good to neighbors, so often that he thought neighbors would be given a share of inheritance [Bukhari 6014].
bubbles: He tied it to faith itself: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day shouldn't harm their neighbor [Bukhari 6018].
That includes neighbors who aren't Muslim. Allah doesn't forbid kindness and fairness to people who live in peace with you [Q 60:8].

screens.prompt: Who counts as a neighbor you should treat well?

options.text: Everyone living near you, Muslim or not
options.feedback: Right. Kindness and fairness to peaceful neighbors of any faith is something Allah loves [Q 60:8].
Not quite. Islam's care for neighbors isn't limited by religion [Q 60:8].

options.text: Only the ones who are kind to you first
options.feedback: Not quite. You can go first, and even answer rudeness with something better [Q 41:34].

screens.situation: Ana's new neighbors play loud music until 1 a.m. on weeknights. She gets up for Fajr (the dawn prayer) and is exhausted.

options.text: Knock on a weekend afternoon, introduce herself, bring something sweet, and ask kindly if they could keep it down after 11
options.feedback: Yes. Neighbors first, request second. Kind and direct usually works, and starts a relationship.

options.text: Tape an angry note to their door
options.feedback: Not quite. Notes feel hostile and start a feud. A face and a friendly tone go much further.

options.text: Call the landlord or police the first night
options.feedback: Sometimes that's needed, but as a first move it skips the chance to just talk. Start kind; escalate if it keeps up.

options.text: Say nothing and quietly resent them for months
options.feedback: Not quite. Silent resentment hurts both of you. A calm request is fair to them and to you.

screens.text: **This is da'wah too.** **Da'wah** means inviting people to Islam. Most of it never involves a speech.
bubbles: It's the coworker who never steals credit, the neighbor who shovels both driveways, the classmate who does their share of the project.
People remember how a Muslim treated them long after they forget what one said [Revealed Path ch. 23].

screens.prompt: Everyday da'wah, or a sales pitch?

items.text: Never stealing credit for a coworker's work
items.why: Honesty at work speaks louder than any speech.

items.text: Shoveling both driveways after a snowstorm
items.why: A quiet kindness your neighbor will remember.

items.text: Doing your full share of the group project
items.why: Being reliable is part of good character, and classmates notice.

items.text: Attaching a lecture about Islam to every favor you do
items.why: Kindness isn't a tactic. Be kind because Allah loves it, full stop [Field Guide ch. 17].

cards.back: A smile and a hello to the neighbor you barely know. Every good deed is charity [Bukhari 6021].
On Eid (the two yearly celebrations), bring a plate of food next door, or treats to work. It opens questions in the nicest way.

cards.front: Return the bad with something better
cards.back: A coworker is cold or rude? Respond with something better, and enemies can become close friends [Q 41:34].
On time, honest with the hours, keeps their word. Coworkers notice.

screens.situation: At work, Tyler's team goes out to a bar for drinks every Friday. He's skipped every time, and lately he's noticed he isn't included in other things either.

options.text: Suggest a team lunch or coffee he can join, and show up warmly to the events that aren't about drinking
options.feedback: Yes. He keeps his line on alcohol and still builds the relationships. Most teams welcome a lunch idea.

options.text: Keep skipping and stop trying, since they clearly don't get it
options.feedback: Not quite. Pulling back completely can leave him isolated at work. Offer another way to connect.

options.text: Give a talk at the next meeting about why alcohol is forbidden
options.feedback: Not quite. Nobody asked for a lecture. A simple "I don't drink, but I'd love to do lunch" is enough.

screens.text: **You're not the spokesperson for two billion people.** You'll have grumpy days and make mistakes, and that's fine. You don't need to be perfect to represent Islam well.
bubbles: Just be decent, honest, and quick to apologize when you get it wrong.
And don't turn every kindness into a sales pitch. Be kind because Allah loves it, full stop [Field Guide ch. 17].

chips: My coworker keeps asking about Islam. How much should I say?
Can I go to a coworker's party if there's alcohol?
How do I give my neighbors food for Eid without it being awkward?
A neighbor is hostile because I'm Muslim. What do I do?

screens.text: One small kindness, no religion talk needed.
steps: Do one kind thing for a neighbor, coworker or classmate: a greeting, help with a task, or something sweet
screens.optional_extra: Learn the name of one neighbor you don't know yet.

screens.text: Being good to neighbors and coworkers, Muslim or not, is part of faith, and it's the da'wah most people will ever see.
You don't need to say much. Just keep showing up kind.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Jibril kept urging kindness to neighbors [Bukhari 6014]; a believer doesn't harm their neighbor [Bukhari 6018].
- Kindness and justice to non-Muslims who live in peace with you are encouraged; Allah loves the just [Q 60:8].
- Respond to bad with what is better [Q 41:34]. Every good deed is charity [Bukhari 6021].
- Muslims are meant to live engaged in their wider society, not isolated, as good citizens and examples [Revealed Path ch. 22–23].
- Don't preach at people or judge non-Muslims by Islamic standards; live it and answer when asked [Field Guide ch. 17].

**Likely questions**
- *"Coworker asks about Islam."* Answer briefly and honestly, about what it means to you; offer more if they're curious; it's fine to say "I don't know, I'll find out" (link Day 71 for tough questions).
- *"Parties with alcohol?"* Give the general picture: Muslims avoid alcohol [Q 5:90], and a hadith tells believers not to sit at a table where alcohol is being passed around [Tirmidhi 2801, hasan per al-Albani]; suggest alternatives (lunch, coffee, leaving early before drinks). For their specific workplace situation, offer "Ask my imam."
- *"Eid food to neighbors?"* Simple: a plate, a note ("It's our holiday, Eid, and we wanted to share"), no obligation.
- *"Hostile neighbor."* Stay calm, document anything threatening, don't retaliate; link Day 52 (Islamophobia) and CAIR for rights. Safety rule if there's a threat.

**Escalate:** harassment or threats from a neighbor or coworker (safety rule; Day 52 resources); workplace religious-accommodation disputes (mentor, CAIR); specific rulings on work events (imam).

**Don't**
- Don't frame kindness as a tactic to convert people.
- Don't encourage the convert to cut off non-Muslim friends or coworkers.
